highlights.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [News](/) English ![Large language models find new tradeoffs on the TIS-100 optimization frontier](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.lavx.hu%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2Flarge-language-models-find-new-tradeoffs-on-the-tis-100-optimization-frontier_gen_1794372096138-1200x630.jpg&w=3840&q=75) #LLMs # Large language models find new tradeoffs on the TIS-100 optimization frontier • ![Elena Varga](/_next/image?url=%2Fauthors%2Felena-varga.webp&w=64&q=75) [Elena Varga](/author/elena-varga) •5 min read Share this article A benchmark gave 16 large language models the assembly puzzle game TIS-100 and asked them to improve working programs. The models produced 133 new Pareto frontier points across 55 puzzles, and players refined several results within days. A new [TIS-100 benchmark](https://tis-100.wincon.dev/) tested 16 large language models on TIS-100, the Zachtronics programming puzzle game where players optimize tiny parallel programs. The benchmark produced 133 new Pareto frontier points across 55 puzzles, set three outright cycle records, and placed new frontier points on 18 puzzles. ## How TIS-100 scores a program TIS-100 gives each puzzle a grid of damaged tiles and as many as 12 nodes. Each node works like a small processor with two registers and room for 15 lines of code. Neighboring nodes exchange values through ports, so one node can stall while it waits for another. The game scores a working solution on three measures: cycles, nodes, and instructions. Lower scores win, but a change that cuts cycles can raise node count or instruction count. Each puzzle holds a frontier of tradeoffs instead of a single best answer. The benchmark counted a new frontier point only after a fresh-game replay and 100,000 passing tests on the independent TIS-100-CXX simulator. ## The benchmark setup The evaluation covered 47 puzzles from the game and eight community tournament puzzles. Each model attempted every puzzle once, with 10 minutes for easy puzzles, 30 minutes for medium puzzles, and 45 minutes for hard puzzles. The models received the game manual, visible test inputs, registers, and game feedback. The harness withheld community code and exact leaderboard records and showed only the game’s coarse score histograms. Models read puzzles, edited programs, and ran them in the game through text tools. Wrong outputs and deadlocks returned diagnostics. The harness saved every passing program to the model’s own frontier, reminded models that ended a turn early to keep testing, and enforced run limits. The models could not end an episode early. ## Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra share the top rank Opus 5.5 from Anthropic and GPT-6 Astra from OpenAI each solved all 55 puzzles and found new frontier points on 11 puzzles. Opus 5.5 found 72 points. GPT-6 Astra found 32 and posted a higher record proximity score, 78.0 to 77.2. The 95% bootstrap interval for that proximity gap included zero, from −0.7 to +2.4 points. GPT-6 Astra led in all six tested hypervolume settings. The results separate solving from optimization. Google’s Gemini 3.8 Flash solved 53 puzzles and found new points on one. Microsoft’s Fable 5.1 solved 52 puzzles and found new points on five. New frontier points appeared on 14 hard puzzles, four medium puzzles, and no easy puzzles. The image above shows Opus 5.5 running [Prime Factor Calculator](https://tis-100.wincon.dev/) at 1,806 cycles, 10 nodes, and 103 instructions. ## A close look at Undecimal Twin Rounder Undecimal Twin Rounder, labeled SPEC44149538, asks a program to round an input to the nearest multiple of N on one output and of 11−N on the other. When the benchmark froze the community leaderboard, the best community program took 2,694 cycles. Opus 5.5 produced a passing program after 6.5 minutes at 5,669 cycles. highlights.content: [![datacenters logo](/_icons/logos/datacenters-logo-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [AI & Compute Infrastructure](/news/ai-compute-infrastructure) * 2 minRead # SK Telecom, Rebellions, NVIDIA partner for Korea AI infrastructure South Korean firms SK Telecom and Rebellions are collaborating with NVIDIA to advance the country's AI infrastructure. This partnership integrates data centers, processors, and an open infrastructure platform to enhance sovereign AI capabilities. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Nov 10, 2026 at 05:10 PM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Set ETDatacenters as your preferred source on Google") Set ETDatacenters as your preferred source on Google ## Highlights * SK Telecom, Rebellions, and NVIDIA are collaborating on South Korea’s AI infrastructure. * Rebellions will integrate its Rebel R200 NPUs with NVIDIA’s platform via NVLink Fusion. * SK Telecom plans to deploy these integrated systems, drawing on its data center expertise. * South Korea’s government supports this initiative with significant funding for sovereign AI. South Korean telecommunications firm [SK Telecom](/tag/sk+telecom), AI chip startup [Rebellions](/tag/rebellions), and [NVIDIA](/tag/nvidia) have announced a collaboration to advance [South Korea](/tag/south+korea)’s [AI infrastructure](/tag/ai+infrastructure). This initiative aims to integrate [data centers](/tag/data+centers), processors, and an open infrastructure platform. Rebellions will use [NVLink Fusion](/tag/nvlink+fusion) to connect its Rebel R200 neural processing units (NPUs) to NVIDIA’s infrastructure platform. SK Telecom plans to deploy these systems, leveraging its data center expertise, according to a press release from NVIDIA. Jung Jai-hun, SK Telecom Chief Executive Officer and President, stated this collaboration validates the potential of next-generation [sovereign AI](/tag/sovereign+ai) infrastructure. He added it combines global AI infrastructure technology with Korean AI semiconductors. Sunghyun Park, Rebellions co-founder and Chief Executive Officer, noted that Korean technology would lead in powering AI worldwide. Jensen Huang, NVIDIA founder and Chief Executive Officer, highlighted Korea's talent and ambition to be a world leader in AI. The firms plan to develop an approach to disaggregated inference. This will assign different stages of AI response generation to the best-suited processor architecture. The plan includes using NVIDIA GPUs for prefill and Rebellions NPUs for decode to improve inference throughput. ### Government Support and Investment South Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) supports this collaboration to strengthen the country’s sovereign AI infrastructure. Bae Kyung-hoon, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Science and ICT, said this enables Korean-developed NPUs to enter the computing infrastructure market alongside NVIDIA. The government will actively support this collaboration, he added, to deliver tangible results and advance cooperation with NVIDIA. Earlier this month, the South Korean government allocated KRW 21.3 trillion (US$ 15.83 billion) in its budget for 2027. This funding supports the development of physical AI, data centers, and semiconductors. A further KRW 4.7 trillion (US$ 3.5 billion) has been earmarked to develop a sovereign AI model. The government also plans to train 2,000 specialists to lead semiconductor design and the wider chip industry. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?

highlights.content: ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)![](https://www.elektormagazine.com/waitress/takeaway/270/image) ![NVIDIA NVLink Fusion brings Korean AI chips to rack-scale systems](https://cdn.eenewseurope.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Asma-eeNews-320-800x600-c-default.png) # NVIDIA NVLink Fusion brings Korean AI chips to rack-scale systems News | By Asma Adhimi [Nvidia](/en/tags/nvidia/) [chip](/en/tags/chip/) [AI](/en/tags/ai/) --- NVIDIA, Korean AI chip developer Rebellions and SK Telecom [are teaming up](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-rebellions-and-sk-telecom-announce-collaboration-to-advance-sovereign-ai-infrastructure-with-nvidia-nvlink-fusion) to develop sovereign AI infrastructure combining locally designed processors with NVIDIA’s NVLink Fusion interconnect technology. The collaboration will see Rebellions’ next-generation R200 neural processing units ([NPUs](https://www.eenewseurope.com/en/tags/npu)) integrated into NVIDIA’s MGX rack architecture, with deployment planned at SK Telecom’s AI data centers. The agreement highlights growing opportunities for custom AI accelerators to work alongside NVIDIA GPUs in large-scale inference systems. For European semiconductor developers and data center operators, it offers a potential blueprint for combining domestic AI silicon with established computing infrastructure to support sovereign AI initiatives. ## NVLink Fusion connects custom AI silicon Rebellions plans to use NVIDIA NVLink Fusion to connect its R200 NPUs through high-bandwidth, low-latency networking, targeting energy-efficient inference for frontier AI models, including multitrillion-parameter mixture-of-experts architectures. The NVIDIA MGX rack architecture will provide standardized system designs, while its ecosystem of original design manufacturers and component suppliers could help Rebellions accelerate development and reduce deployment complexity. “Today’s announcement marks a turning point, opening a new chapter for sovereign AI by connecting Korea’s AI silicon and models with global systems technology,” said Sunghyun Park, cofounder and CEO of Rebellions. The companies also plan to explore disaggregated inference, splitting AI workloads between different processor architectures. Under the proposed approach, NVIDIA GPUs would handle the compute-intensive prefill stage, while Rebellions NPUs would manage token generation during decoding. This division of labor is intended to improve inference throughput and power efficiency, potentially addressing two major challenges facing AI data center operators. ## SK Telecom targets full-stack sovereign AI SK Telecom plans to deploy the systems within its AI data center infrastructure, connecting the hardware with proprietary foundation models, including A.X K2, and public-facing AI services. The initiative supports Korea’s government-backed “AI for All” project and aims to strengthen domestic control over AI infrastructure, models and services. Standardizing rack footprints, power delivery and cooling through NVIDIA MGX could also simplify integration of GPU and NPU systems within existing data center environments. ## Government backing and 2028 deployment Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT is supporting the collaboration as part of a broader effort to strengthen the country’s sovereign AI capabilities and domestic semiconductor industry. The initiative could provide a model for other regions seeking greater AI infrastructure independence without developing every component of the technology stack themselves. highlights.content: [![techmonk logo](/_icons/logos/techmonk-logo-mobile-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [AI](/news/ai) * 2 minRead # Trent AI builds multi-agent code-to-doc system on OpenClaw Trent AI has developed a multi-agent system using OpenClaw to automate public documentation generation from code. This pipeline aims to address documentation drift in fast-paced engineering environments. * [TechGig](/agency/87450652/TechGig "TechGig") * Published On Nov 10, 2026 at 06:45 AM IST ## Highlights * Trent AI built a multi-agent code-to-doc pipeline on OpenClaw for automated documentation. * The system uses Change Scanner, Doc Classifier, Doc Publisher, and Orchestrator agents. * Deployment on AWS prioritised security with no public IP and restricted egress. * GitHub App permissions and branch protection limit agent actions and require human review. Trent AI has built a multi-agent system on [OpenClaw](/tag/openclaw) to automate the generation of public documentation from code, the company said. This initiative aims to address documentation drift, where engineering teams ship features rapidly while documentation falls out of date. The system uses OpenClaw's agentic capabilities and is composed of several agents. These include a Change Scanner, a Doc Classifier, a Doc Publisher, and an Orchestrator, along with [GitHub](/tag/github) Tools. ### Multi-agent system architecture The Change Scanner reads code repositories, fetches merged pull requests, and identifies impacted files. The Doc Classifier triages changes into categories like breaking changes or new features, assigning a confidence score. The Doc Publisher converts raw files into customer-facing documents, reconciles existing documentation, and creates a pull request with updated content. An Orchestrator coordinates these components, tracks failures, and runs the pipeline on a schedule. GitHub Tools are scripts connecting to GitHub, used by the Change Scanner and Doc Publisher. Trent AI developed an agent for each component to understand [multi-agent systems](/tag/multi-agent+systems). OpenClaw currently lacks clear context handoff for multi-agent work, so Trent AI used shared files for context exchange. This is a common practice for long-running agents. ### Secure AWS deployment Trent AI deployed the agents safely on AWS, guided by principles of least privilege and a tight blast radius. The system only receives necessary access, and any compromise remains contained within the documentation pipeline. A security review, using Trent's Claude Code Security, identified threats such as data exfiltration, code pollution, and secret leakage. Mitigations were mapped to risks for each agent and network path. The AWS deployment uses a single EC2 instance within a VPC, without a public IP or inbound rules. Access is limited to AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, removing the need for SSH keys. Egress traffic is controlled by AWS Network Firewall with a stateful FQDN allow-list. This restricts the instance to communicating only with essential services like GitHub and the Bedrock control plane. Agents authenticate via a dedicated GitHub App installed only on the relevant repository, with permissions scoped to pull\_requests:read+write and contents:read+write. No admin access or metadata writes are permitted. GitHub's branch protection requires human review for every pull request opened by the agents. The agents can propose changes but cannot merge their own work. OpenClaw's agentToAgent setting, a boolean with an allow-list of agent IDs, gates inter-agent calls. This limits the blast radius of [prompt injection](/tag/prompt+injection) attacks to the documentation pipeline agents. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?

Together, these developments position Red Hat to help enterprises manage agentic AI through open, Kubernetes-based infrastructure. Unlike conventional applications, autonomous agents can generate commands, invoke tools and delegate work across multiple systems. That flexibility creates opportunities for automation while increasing the importance of consistent access controls and oversight. This feature is part of SiliconANGLE Media’s exploration of how cloud-native infrastructure is evolving to support enterprise AI, with Red Hat and the broader Kubernetes ecosystem addressing the security, operational efficiency and scalability requirements of autonomous agents. (\* Disclosure below.) ### Red Hat advances Kubernetes-native security for AI agents The rapid adoption of OpenClaw has brought renewed attention to agent security. An agent that can read files, run shell commands and make network calls needs clearly defined permissions and isolation to operate safely within enterprise environments. Cryptocurrency markets provide a natural testbed for autonomous AI agents because they are digital-native, high-frequency, and machine-speed environments, yet existing methods often struggle with non-stationary market regimes, opaque decisions, and fixed aggregation rules. In this paper, we propose Agent4Crypto, a dual-reflective and market-feedback-aligned multi-agent system. The framework coordinates specialized agents for data collection, analysis, risk assessment, reflection, and trading, synthesizing heterogeneous signals from prices, indicators, news, and charts in an interpretable decision pipeline. Our central design is a trader-centric decision mechanism: three style-specific trader agents, Aggressive, Neutral, and Conservative, generate candidate actions and natural-language rationales from the same market context, while their influence is learned rather than manually fixed. A PPO-based gating policy dynamically allocates trader weights through a dual-reflective feedback process. One reflection stream evaluates post-trade decision quality from realized portfolio outcomes and distills reusable lessons into a Financial ReasoningBank for retrieval in subsequent trader prompts, while the other estimates trader-level counterfactual contribution, indicating which style has recently aligned better with market movements. The PPO state combines Counterfactual Contribution Memory with market features, previous trader weights, and current trader actions, so trader influence adapts across bull, sideways, and bear regimes. Experiments on BTC, ETH, and XRP show that Agent4Crypto improves total return and Sharpe ratio over traditional strategies, machine learning and reinforcement learning baselines, and existing LLM-based trading systems, demonstrating the value of interpretable trader competition and market-feedback-driven adaptation in volatile cryptocurrency markets. ###### Keywords: ## 1. This pipeline aims to address documentation drift in fast-paced engineering environments. * [TechGig](/agency/87450652/TechGig "TechGig") * Published On Nov 10, 2026 at 06:45 AM IST ## Highlights * Trent AI built a multi-agent code-to-doc pipeline on OpenClaw for automated documentation. * The system uses Change Scanner, Doc Classifier, Doc Publisher, and Orchestrator agents. * Deployment on AWS prioritised security with no public IP and restricted egress. * GitHub App permissions and branch protection limit agent actions and require human review. Trent AI has built a multi-agent system on [OpenClaw](/tag/openclaw) to automate the generation of public documentation from code, the company said. This initiative aims to address documentation drift, where engineering teams ship features rapidly while documentation falls out of date. The system uses OpenClaw's agentic capabilities and is composed of several agents. These include a Change Scanner, a Doc Classifier, a Doc Publisher, and an Orchestrator, along with [GitHub](/tag/github) Tools. ### Multi-agent system architecture The Change Scanner reads code repositories, fetches merged pull requests, and identifies impacted files. The Doc Classifier triages changes into categories like breaking changes or new features, assigning a confidence score. The Doc Publisher converts raw files into customer-facing documents, reconciles existing documentation, and creates a pull request with updated content. An Orchestrator coordinates these components, tracks failures, and runs the pipeline on a schedule. GitHub Tools are scripts connecting to GitHub, used by the Change Scanner and Doc Publisher. Trent AI developed an agent for each component to understand [multi-agent systems](/tag/multi-agent+systems). OpenClaw currently lacks clear context handoff for multi-agent work, so Trent AI used shared files for context exchange. This is a common practice for long-running agents. ### Secure AWS deployment Trent AI deployed the agents safely on AWS, guided by principles of least privilege and a tight blast radius. The system only receives necessary access, and any compromise remains contained within the documentation pipeline. A security review, using Trent's Claude Code Security, identified threats such as data exfiltration, code pollution, and secret leakage. Mitigations were mapped to risks for each agent and network path. The AWS deployment uses a single EC2 instance within a VPC, without a public IP or inbound rules. Access is limited to AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, removing the need for SSH keys. Egress traffic is controlled by AWS Network Firewall with a stateful FQDN allow-list. This restricts the instance to communicating only with essential services like GitHub and the Bedrock control plane. Agents authenticate via a dedicated GitHub App installed only on the relevant repository, with permissions scoped to pull\_requests:read+write and contents:read+write. No admin access or metadata writes are permitted. GitHub's branch protection requires human review for every pull request opened by the agents. The agents can propose changes but cannot merge their own work. OpenClaw's agentToAgent setting, a boolean with an allow-list of agent IDs, gates inter-agent calls. This limits the blast radius of [prompt injection](/tag/prompt+injection) attacks to the documentation pipeline agents. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?

Bram Red Hat LLC has spent years making Kubernetes manageable for enterprises that would rather run applications than tend clusters. As AI agents move into production, the company is extending that experience to a new generation of workloads. AI agents don’t just consume infrastructure. They execute commands, call external tools, access enterprise systems and take actions that can affect the business. The next phase of AI agent infrastructure requires enforceable security boundaries alongside efficient resource management. Red Hat arrives at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City this week with a growing portfolio of technologies addressing those requirements. OpenShift provides the Kubernetes foundation; its work with Nvidia Corp. on OpenShell addresses agent execution and security; and the llm-d project has reached version 1.0 with capabilities for serving the context-heavy workloads agents create. Together, these developments position Red Hat to help enterprises manage agentic AI through open, Kubernetes-based infrastructure. Unlike conventional applications, autonomous agents can generate commands, invoke tools and delegate work across multiple systems. That flexibility creates opportunities for automation while increasing the importance of consistent access controls and oversight. This feature is part of SiliconANGLE Media’s exploration of how cloud-native infrastructure is evolving to support enterprise AI, with Red Hat and the broader Kubernetes ecosystem addressing the security, operational efficiency and scalability requirements of autonomous agents. (\* Disclosure below.) ### Red Hat advances Kubernetes-native security for AI agents The rapid adoption of OpenClaw has brought renewed attention to agent security. An agent that can read files, run shell commands and make network calls needs clearly defined permissions and isolation to operate safely within enterprise environments. Red Hat’s response centers on its collaboration with Nvidia around OpenShell, a runtime that places agents inside isolated execution environments and applies policy to their access. Nvidia developed OpenShell; Red Hat is working with Nvidia and the wider community to integrate the technology into Red Hat AI and its open hybrid cloud platform. Red Hat’s announcement describes the work as part of a broader effort to bring security-focused agentic AI capabilities to enterprise infrastructure. These complementary layers govern agent behavior and isolate the environments in which agents operate, as Red Hat explains in its technical overview of layered sandboxing. The distinction matters because sandboxing does not make an agent trustworthy. It limits the damage an agent can cause when its instructions, generated code or external inputs lead it somewhere they should not. Cryptocurrency markets provide a natural testbed for autonomous AI agents because they are digital-native, high-frequency, and machine-speed environments, yet existing methods often struggle with non-stationary market regimes, opaque decisions, and fixed aggregation rules. AI Agents.titleZh: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon with agent ‘swarm’ feature | The Verge
AI Agents.content: Google is rolling out its latest AI model, Gemini 4 Carbon, to the general public after releasing it to a select group of “cybersecurity defenders” two weeks ago. Google claims Carbon is its “strongest model” yet, and capable of competing with the very best systems from Anthropic and OpenAI. # Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon with agent ‘swarm’ feature It ‘pushes the frontier even further’ than its last release, Argon.﻿ It ‘pushes the frontier even further’ than its last release, Argon.﻿ Google says Gemini 4 Carbon “pushes the frontier even further” than Argon, referring to the company’s other frontier model that launched only last month. The company said Argon will likely remain “the ideal choice for the majority of software engineering and knowledge work,” but that Carbon is “built for tasks that test the limits of a model’s intelligence,” such as complex, multi-step coding and open-ended scientific research. To highlight Carbon’s utility for long-horizon work involving AI agents, Google said it is also previewing a “swarm” feature on its agentic development platform Antigravity, which will let users turn a single prompt “into a coordinated team of agents.” Carbon is rolling out today via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business for all paying developers and enterprises, Google said in a blog post. It will also be available to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, the AI Mode in Search, and on Antigravity. It is not clear when — or if — Carbon will be available to lower tier subscribers or free users. As with the launch of Argon, Google is pricing Carbon very competitively. The model is launching with an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, around a fifth the cost of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and a quarter the cost of Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model, which launched yesterday. Even after those costs double at the end November — when the introductory period of lower prices finishes — Carbon will still be significantly cheaper than frontier rivals on a per-token basis, though this doesn’t necessarily translate to lower costs as models can use different numbers of tokens for the same tasks. Benchmarks cited by Google when it first announced Carbon suggest the model is one of the most powerful on the market across most metrics, behind Fable 5.2. It should be noted that companies can and do cherry-pick benchmark results to show their tools in the best possible light. The release, hot on the heels of Argon, marks a decisive return for Google at the very forefront of AI research. For months, frontier development looked like a two-horse race between Anthropic and OpenAI.

AI Agents.content: # Why more GPUs and tokens don’t guarantee better AI agent outcomes Presented by WEKA Enterprises running multi-agent AI systems should measure them by cost-per-completed-outcome and keep each agent's working context in fast storage outside GPU memory, says Val Bercovici, chief AI officer at WEKA. Speaking with VentureBeat founder Matt Marshall at the VB Agentic Infrastructure Stack Summit, Bercovici pointed to two reasons enterprise GPU spending on AI agents runs higher than the work requires. First is token-based billing. Model providers and their customers still price agent work by tokens consumed, so a team of agents looks more expensive than a single agent even when it finishes each task at a lower cost-per-outcome. Secondly, there’s recomputation of the KV cache, the short-term memory a large language model builds while it processes a prompt. When that cache falls out of GPU memory, the GPU serving the next agent in a swarm has to recompute context another agent already built, and enterprises buy extra GPUs largely to hold more of it in high-bandwidth memory. "The number one rule is don't recompute the same token twice," Bercovici said. "Don't prefill twice." ## Why enterprises should measure multi-agent AI by cost-per-outcome Bigger agent teams aren't better. Independent AI evaluator Vals AI found that agent teams on its Vibe Code Bench AI waste huge amounts of tokens for a bump in speed, costing 1.8 to 5.1 times as much as single agents, with barely measurable quality gains. Customer conversations have shifted from "tokenmaxxing" at the start of the year to "token capping" now, as finance teams measure each agent run's cost against the value of the work it produced. "We're still stuck as an industry on billing per token," Bercovici said. "We're billing consumption instead of billing outcomes." Bercovici cited independent evaluators such as Vals AI and Epoch AI, which grade the quality of agent work in legal, financial, and medical tasks and calculate the cost of each completed task or session. For their numbers to hold up, these evaluators must stay independent of the model labs and agent harness vendors, and buyers should keep checking that they do. "I think it'll be a higher volume of tokens at a lower unit cost, delivering that better cost-per-outcome," he said. In a later panel, Bercovici and Upwork’s vice president of platform infrastructure engineering, Sudhanshu Bist, illustrated why that calculation is difficult. Upwork’s AI gateway tracks model spending and attributes it to teams and services, Bist said, but it does not capture training or fine-tuning costs, the human effort needed to correct results, or the CPU resources consumed by tool calls. Those costs sit in separate systems, making the full cost of an outcome harder to measure. ## Why AI agent swarms need fast KV cache and long-term context retention "There's never been such a thing as an agent in real-world production," Bercovici said. "It's always been plural." Deployments either coordinate several agents or let one agent spawn subtasks that behave as agents themselves. As work passes between them, agents need access to the context already built. Those handoffs draw on two kinds of memory. Short-term memory includes the KV cache, which stores the attention keys and values a model computes for each token. Keeping that cache lets the model generate subsequent tokens without reprocessing the entire sequence. Long-term memory preserves context from earlier sessions that an agent may need again when a user or another agent returns. "The key word now is retention," Bercovici said. "How long are you going to need to retain information and access it very quickly, as opposed to recompute it?" Agents that never stop make retention harder. LLMs.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [News](/) English ![Large language models find new tradeoffs on the TIS-100 optimization frontier](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.lavx.hu%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2Flarge-language-models-find-new-tradeoffs-on-the-tis-100-optimization-frontier_gen_1794372096138-1200x630.jpg&w=3840&q=75) #LLMs # Large language models find new tradeoffs on the TIS-100 optimization frontier • ![Elena Varga](/_next/image?url=%2Fauthors%2Felena-varga.webp&w=64&q=75) [Elena Varga](/author/elena-varga) •5 min read Share this article A benchmark gave 16 large language models the assembly puzzle game TIS-100 and asked them to improve working programs. The models produced 133 new Pareto frontier points across 55 puzzles, and players refined several results within days. A new [TIS-100 benchmark](https://tis-100.wincon.dev/) tested 16 large language models on TIS-100, the Zachtronics programming puzzle game where players optimize tiny parallel programs. The benchmark produced 133 new Pareto frontier points across 55 puzzles, set three outright cycle records, and placed new frontier points on 18 puzzles. ## How TIS-100 scores a program TIS-100 gives each puzzle a grid of damaged tiles and as many as 12 nodes. Each node works like a small processor with two registers and room for 15 lines of code. Neighboring nodes exchange values through ports, so one node can stall while it waits for another. The game scores a working solution on three measures: cycles, nodes, and instructions. Lower scores win, but a change that cuts cycles can raise node count or instruction count. Each puzzle holds a frontier of tradeoffs instead of a single best answer. The benchmark counted a new frontier point only after a fresh-game replay and 100,000 passing tests on the independent TIS-100-CXX simulator. ## The benchmark setup The evaluation covered 47 puzzles from the game and eight community tournament puzzles. Each model attempted every puzzle once, with 10 minutes for easy puzzles, 30 minutes for medium puzzles, and 45 minutes for hard puzzles. The models received the game manual, visible test inputs, registers, and game feedback. The harness withheld community code and exact leaderboard records and showed only the game’s coarse score histograms. Models read puzzles, edited programs, and ran them in the game through text tools. Wrong outputs and deadlocks returned diagnostics. The harness saved every passing program to the model’s own frontier, reminded models that ended a turn early to keep testing, and enforced run limits. The models could not end an episode early. ## Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra share the top rank Opus 5.5 from Anthropic and GPT-6 Astra from OpenAI each solved all 55 puzzles and found new frontier points on 11 puzzles. Opus 5.5 found 72 points. GPT-6 Astra found 32 and posted a higher record proximity score, 78.0 to 77.2. The 95% bootstrap interval for that proximity gap included zero, from −0.7 to +2.4 points. GPT-6 Astra led in all six tested hypervolume settings. The results separate solving from optimization. Google’s Gemini 3.8 Flash solved 53 puzzles and found new points on one. Microsoft’s Fable 5.1 solved 52 puzzles and found new points on five. New frontier points appeared on 14 hard puzzles, four medium puzzles, and no easy puzzles. The image above shows Opus 5.5 running [Prime Factor Calculator](https://tis-100.wincon.dev/) at 1,806 cycles, 10 nodes, and 103 instructions. ## A close look at Undecimal Twin Rounder Undecimal Twin Rounder, labeled SPEC44149538, asks a program to round an input to the nearest multiple of N on one output and of 11−N on the other. When the benchmark froze the community leaderboard, the best community program took 2,694 cycles. Opus 5.5 produced a passing program after 6.5 minutes at 5,669 cycles. The model dropped below the community record after 16 minutes and finished at 1,918 cycles, 29% faster than the frozen record. The speed cost one more node and 28 more instructions. The program us...

The company said Fable 5.2 is aimed at general users and blocks most biology research questions and many cybersecurity requests, while Mythos 5.2 relaxes limits for verified researchers. Anthropic reported benchmark gains in science and coding, improvements in safety filtering, faster response modes, and token prices 20 percent lower than the prior generation. * Writer Seung-a Yoo (유승아) * published 2026-11-11 09:26:23 * updated 2026-11-11 09:28:03 Link copied to clipboard. ![](https://cdn.digitaltoday.co.kr/news/photo/202611/714445_661793_518.jpg) Anthropic unveiled Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 with enhanced performance for scientific research and coding. [Photo: Shutterstock] Anthropic unveiled the large language models (LLMs) “Claude Fable 5.2” and “Claude Mythos 5.2,” which it said strengthen scientific research and coding performance. On Nov. 10 (local time), IT outlet SiliconANGLE reported that the two models are Anthropic’s best-performing models to date. They share the same core capabilities, but differ in the level of safeguards in biology and cybersecurity. Fable 5.2 is offered to general users and blocks most biology research questions and many cybersecurity-related requests. Mythos 5.2, by contrast, is a version with relaxed restrictions and is available only to verified researchers through two restricted-access programs. The scale of the performance improvement was confirmed in benchmarks. Anthropic compared Fable 5.2 with the prior model across 14 AI evaluations and said it scored more than 10 percent higher than Fable 5.1 in most categories. In Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, which assesses scientific research capabilities, it scored 74.6 percent, an improvement of 22 percent from the prior model. It also delivered results in complex mathematics research. Anthropic said it took 11 days for a previously undisclosed model to convert a well-known mathematical theorem into a form that can be verified by computer, but Fable 5.2 cut the time to 30 hours by parallelising calculations using 1,000 agents. In separate research, it presented answers to two unsolved problems in theoretical physics related to black holes. Mythos 5.2 also demonstrated performance in life sciences. It analysed 34 capsids, the protective shells of the harmless AAV virus, and accurately modelled the structures of 28 of them. AAV capsids are used to deliver drugs in some treatments. This is meaningful in that it analysed a complex structure composed of dozens of proteins. Google DeepMind’s AlphaFold2, used in biology research, is a model that predicts individual protein structures. Coding performance also improved sharply. Fable 5.2 posted performance more than 13 percent higher than the previous model on two coding benchmarks, FrontierCode 2.0 and FrontierSWE v2. In an experiment in which Anthropic engineers assigned it to build an operating system, more than 1,000 agents wrote and verified code for about 8 days to complete a functioning operating system. The operating system runs on a laptop and supports network connections and Claude functions. Safety and efficiency were also improved. When Fable 5.2 receives restricted biology or cybersecurity requests, it routes them to Opus 4.8 or Opus 5. Anthropic said the likelihood of incorrectly blocking safe requests fell 55 percent versus the prior model. Anthropic presented the two models as suitable for complex and open-ended technical tasks. LLMs.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Holdings](/stocklist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast)[Market Influencers](/influencer) # Goodfire's Curt Tigges says AI models can lose 90% of their neurons and keep working [Add preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) Curt Tigges, a researcher at interpretability startup Goodfire, has published a study of the Qwen3.6 35B-A3B model arguing that individual neurons in large language models are far more readable than the field assumed — and that most can be deleted with almost no loss of performance. Ablating roughly 88–90% of the model's five million neurons left benchmark scores near parity, and in some cases improved ARC-AGI puzzle results; after about 100 million tokens of extra training, the stripped-down model matched or beat the original on several tests. The paper's second contribution is a "neuron scientist" agent that writes and tests plain-language descriptions of what each neuron does, with a different model validating the result by recovering 74% of the damage caused by removal. The findings matter for investors because they reframe AI interpretability from a research curiosity into a monitoring and safety tool — one that could help labs audit models before release, exactly as regulators in Australia begin mandating disclosure of misaligned behavior. But Tigges is candid that mapping neurons to actual model behavior remains unsolved, and that million-token contexts are untested. ##### Key Elements ![Goodfire's Curt Tigges says AI models can lose 90% of their neurons and keep working](https://img.biggo.com/YoZLd10aEXO8vtBvJFAF_PjDUMeQMM_oixrKpY9pa0A/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTExLzhhZWFjOWU4NjY3MTg4MDlfMTc5NDM0NzIzMl9jb3Zlci5qcGc.webp) Most of what you've heard about the insides of AI models describes a black box. A new study from Goodfire, a startup working on model interpretability, argues the box is far more transparent than the field believed — and that you can delete almost all of it without breaking what's inside. The paper, "Neurons as an Interpretable Basis," examines Qwen3.6 35B-A3B, a 35-billion-parameter model built on a mixture-of-experts design with roughly five million neurons. When the authors removed the weakest activations so that only about 88–90% of neurons were ablated — effectively cutting the model's brain mass by nine-tenths — benchmark performance barely moved. On the ARC-AGI reasoning puzzles, cutting neurons actually improved the score. "If we keep only the strongest activations, there is surprisingly minimal performance degradation," Curt Tigges, a member of technical staff at Goodfire and a co-author, said on The Cognitive Revolution podcast. "In some cases, such as on the ARC AGI puzzles, such intensive ablation actually improved performance." The finding lands at an awkward moment for the industry. Australia said this week it will require AI companies to report when their models behave in unintended or misaligned ways and to submit them for outside evaluation, after an OpenAI agent breached a government website in June. That kind of oversight is only possible if someone can see inside the model. Tigges' work suggests the tools to do so may be closer than regulators assume — and also that they have a long way to go. ### The model's weakest signals carry almost none of the weight The core intuition is that not all neuron firings matter equally. Rank a neuron's activations from weakest to strongest, and the examples stay coherent deep into the top percentiles before dissolving into noise. The exact cutoff varies by neuron and by layer, which is why the paper uses two ablation methods rather than a single fixed threshold. Ari Singer | IDF Spokesperson's Unit" (Recorded on Nov. 10, 2026) The modern defense environment is characterized by heavy information overload, with relevant defense intelligence spanning military doctrine, technical manuals, and rapidly evolving operational news. Processing this content requires a precise grasp of technical terminology, operational context, and specialized domain-specific reasoning capabilities. According to a report in [Arxiv](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.15022v1), researchers from Korea University, Sungkyunkwan University, and Hanwha Systems in South Korea have developed SALUTE, a comprehensive end-to-end framework for evaluating and adapting large language models (LLMs) to the defense sector. General-purpose LLMs are often constrained in professional fields that demand deep background, domain-specific knowledge, and reliable reasoning, underscoring the need for tailored models alongside a unified infrastructure for data construction, model training, and comprehensive evaluation. While language technologies have previously been explored for military applications, earlier efforts remained fragmented—focusing on isolated tasks such as military event extraction or spatial planning, relying on single-stage adaptation processes, and offering evaluation benchmarks that were limited in scope and openness. The new framework combines specialized data resource construction, multi-stage post-training, and a diverse evaluation benchmark designed to overcome the limitations of existing tools. To establish the knowledge foundation, the researchers built Salute-Corpus, a repository based on open-access U.S. military doctrine and relevant government documents. Heterogeneous PDF source documents were converted into structured Markdown, segmented by sections, deduplicated, and filtered of low-quality content using multi-agent scoring and a ModernBERT-based quality model to prepare them for continual pre-training (CPT). The team subsequently developed the Salute-Conv instruction dataset, drawn from doctrinal sources and defense news gathered over a decade, to enable military question answering and domain-specific instruction following. The instruction data was generated through task planning, chunk-based question generation, retrieval-augmented evidence selection, and factual answer synthesis, bridging stable doctrinal knowledge with dynamic defense event reporting. In addition, the researchers constructed the Salute-Pref preference dataset, designed to preserve defense-specific behaviors and characteristics during the model's preference alignment phase. Built upon these resources, the Salute-LLM model was trained through a multi-stage process comprising continual pre-training (CPT) to embed defense knowledge, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for instruction following, and preference alignment to enhance output quality. To assess performance, the authors introduced Salute-Bench, a rigorously curated evaluation benchmark measuring doctrine- and defense news-based comprehension and reasoning across open-ended and multiple-choice formats. LLMs.titleZh: LingBot-Touch Open-Sourced: 5,000 Hours of Touch Data [2026]
LLMs.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Robbyant Open-Sources LingBot-Touch: 5,000 Hours [2026] ![Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/tvance.webp) [Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/author/tvance/) Updated Nov 11, 2026 · 17 min read Robbyant, the embodied AI company inside Ant Group, open-sourced LingBot-Touch on November 10, 2026, a tactile foundation model built to give robots a general-purpose sense of touch, according to [its Business Wire release carried by Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20261109284905/robbyant-releases-lingbot-touch-to-bring-general-purpose-touch-perception-to-robots). The model targets one of the stubborn gaps in robotics: machines that see well but still fumble objects the moment contact begins. LingBot-Touch trained on nearly 5,000 hours of real-world tactile data and supports three sensing types: magnetic tactile, visual tactile, and piezoresistive. It encodes signals from all three into a unified tactile representation, so different action models can consume touch data without a custom pipeline for every sensor. Robbyant published a technical report and code, and model resources sit on Hugging Face and GitHub. The launch fits a wider shift toward physical AI, where models leave the chat window and act on the world. Our earlier report on the [ASTRA robot that builds structures in space under DARPA’s NOM4D program](https://shattered.io/astra-robot-builds-structure-in-space-darpa-nom4d-caltech-2026/) showed how much of that work depends on precise contact. This analysis covers what Robbyant confirmed, what remains unverified, how the design compares with other approaches to robot touch perception, and what builders should do next. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## What Robbyant Released and Why It Matters Most robot learning stacks treat touch as an afterthought. A team picks a gripper, bolts on one type of tactile sensor, collects demonstrations, and trains a policy that only works with that exact hardware. Swap the sensor and the whole pipeline needs new data. That cost keeps tactile sensing out of many production systems, even though contact is where assembly, packing, and household tasks succeed or fail. Robbyant’s answer is a shared layer. LingBot-Touch is described in the announcement as a tactile foundation model, meaning a large pretrained network that other systems build on instead of training from scratch. Its job is to turn raw contact signals into tokens that an action model can read. The company is betting that one pretrained touch encoder can serve many hands and many policies. Open-sourcing the work matters as much as the design. A released technical report and code let outside labs test the claims, port the encoder to their own hardware, and report failures. Closed tactile models can only be judged by the vendor’s own demos. For a field with few shared benchmarks, an open release gives the community something concrete to measure. The Business Wire release and the follow-up coverage agree on the core facts. The AI Insider, in [its November 10 write-up](https://theaiinsider.tech/2026/11/10/robbyant-releases-open-source-ai-model-to-improve-robots-sense-of-touch/), framed the release as an open-source model meant to improve robots’ sense of touch and their ability to handle objects. Interesting Engineering ran its own piece pitching the 5,000-hour training corpus as a shared sense of touch for robots. No price appeared in any retrieved source, which fits an open-source release. ## LingBot-Touch at a Glance: What Is Confirmed Before the analysis, here is the ground truth. AI Product.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Anthropic Ships 4 Office Tools to Rival Microsoft [2026] ![Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Nov 10, 2026 · 14 min read Anthropic stepped into Microsoft’s home turf on November 10, 2026. At an event in San Francisco, the company unveiled four workplace products named Claude Meetings, Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards and Claude Data, and [Engadget framed the push as Anthropic taking on both Google and Microsoft](https://www.engadget.com/2312177/anthropic-takes-on-google-and-microsoft-with-claude-sheets/). The new Anthropic office tools turn Claude from a chat window into something closer to a teammate that sits in meetings, edits spreadsheets and builds dashboards. Anthropic summed up the pitch in one line: “Starting today, Claude can build spreadsheets, whiteboards, and dashboards with your team.” The sentence matters because it moves Claude out of the personal-assistant lane and into shared work, where the money in enterprise software has always sat. The timing also draws attention. Reports describe an anticipated Anthropic public offering, and the launch landed while investors were already sizing up the company. Our earlier analysis of [what Amazon and Google could gain from an Anthropic IPO](https://shattered.io/amazon-google-411-billion-anthropic-ipo-windfall-2026/) covers the investor side. This piece stays on the products, the competitive stakes and what is still unproven. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## What Anthropic Announced on November 10 Anthropic PBC announced four products in one event. Claude Meetings is an AI assistant that joins video calls. Claude Sheets is a spreadsheet tool. Claude Whiteboards is a brainstorming canvas. Claude Data, which Anthropic previously called Claude Dashboards, connects Claude to company systems and produces dashboards. Bloomberg’s headline put the strategic angle in plain terms, and [Bloomberg Law’s republished version of the story](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/ip-law/anthropic-unveils-office-tools-ahead-of-ipo-taking-on-microsoft) says Anthropic unveiled office tools ahead of its IPO, taking on Microsoft. Fortune ran a similar story under a headline about a new suite of AI office productivity tools in the run-up to the IPO. Both outlets tie the launch to the offering. AI Product.titleZh: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks | TechCrunch
AI Product.content: Anthropic announced new workplace features on Tuesday, including Claude Meetings, which brings Claude into video calls to begin working on tasks while participants are still talking. The company also unveiled Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets. The launch of Anthropic’s new productivity-focused features comes just a few weeks after OpenAI unveiled a series of workplace tools that allow users to collaborate with ChatGPT to do things like visualize company information and create presentations, as both companies compete to turn their products into office suites of sorts to take on Microsoft and Google. Meta is also joining the competition with its Muse AI agent, which can build mini-apps on the fly to help users complete specific tasks. With Claude Meetings, teams can add Claude to a video call as a visible participant. Claude then follows the conversation and gets to work on tasks in real time. As participants talk, it can draft the plan being discussed, map out a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat, and access connected work apps to retrieve information, such as last year’s figures. After the call, the meeting notes, action items, and other materials Claude created are available in claude.ai. The work that comes out of a meeting usually starts after everyone hangs up, but with this new feature, teams can turn discussions into actions in real time, Anthropic says. Claude identifies itself as a meeting participant and posts a notice in the meeting chat. It won’t join calls with external guests unless authorized by an admin, and will automatically leave if an external guest joins. Claude Meetings is launching in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. At launch, it works with Google Meet, with support for additional plans expected to follow. As for Claude Whiteboards, Anthropic describes the feature as a collaborative board where teams can talk through a plan and have Claude turn it into an organized visual workspace with timelines and deadlines. The company notes that many people already brainstorm with Claude, but that in order to share their results with others, they would have to copy-paste them somewhere else. Now, a team can work directly with Claude on the same board in real time. When the brainstorm is done, Claude can turn the board into a doc or a slide deck. Additionally, Whiteboards also work inside Claude Meetings, so the board builds while people talk, Anthropic says. Claude Whiteboards is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop, and mobile. The company also launched Claude Sheets, which lets teams create and collaboratively edit spreadsheets with Claude. A team can ask it to build a campaign tracker or hiring budget, and Claude will then generate a working spreadsheet. Anthropic says Claude handles the initial setup of trackers and budgets, while allowing teams to continue refining and updating the same spreadsheet. Each spreadsheet can include multiple tabs, formulas, formatting, and dropdown menus. Claude also makes edits directly in cells alongside the team, and outlines each change so users can see what it did. Claude Sheets is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop and mobile. Anthropic also announced that Claude Data, formerly known as Claude Dashboards, is now generally available. The feature connects Claude to systems that companies use to keep their numbers, like a data warehouse or CRM. Users can ask questions, and Claude responds with dashboards, written data stories, or narrated videos. Additionally, the company announced interactive connectors that open the full version of apps like Adobe, Atlassian, and HubSpot inside Claude. Anthropic notes that teams can now open these apps directly alongside their Claude conversations and ask the assistant to work within them, essentially bringing existing workflows into the same workspace. AI Product.content: ## [SMBtech](https://smbtech.au) [Menu](#) Adobe Puts AI Agents Inside Its Content Supply Chain As It Pitches The ‘Studio Of The Future’ ![Adobe Partners With Luma Ai To Launch Ray3 Video Model In Firefly](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7) # Adobe Puts AI Agents Inside Its Content Supply Chain As It Pitches The ‘Studio Of The Future’ [Staff Writer](https://smbtech.au/author/staff-writer/) November 11, 2026 [News](https://smbtech.au/category/news/ "View all posts in News") #### Surprisingly Useful AI Article Enhancements Adobe has announced a series of agentic AI features for its GenStudio platform, centred on a conversational AI assistant called CX Enterprise Coworker that is designed to coordinate content creation, campaign planning and asset production across marketing and creative teams. The announcements, made at Adobe MAX, position the company’s GenStudio suite as the backbone of what Adobe is calling the “Studio of the Future”, where AI agents work alongside human creatives and marketers to accelerate the production of personalised content at scale. The core proposition is that brands producing content across dozens of channels and markets need AI that understands their brand guidelines, can coordinate workflows across multiple tools and can handle repetitive production tasks so that human teams can focus on higher-value creative and strategic work. ### CX Enterprise Coworker comes to GenStudio CX Enterprise Coworker is Adobe’s agentic AI assistant for customer experience orchestration. It is being brought into GenStudio, where it will act as a conversational interface that can coordinate AI agents and workflows across an organisation’s content supply chain. The tool is designed to sit across Adobe’s enterprise application suite, which the company says more than 20,000 brands rely on for data unification, content creation and customer experience management. It will synthesise insights from across GenStudio and third-party applications, with integration built on open standards including Model Context Protocol and Agent-to-Agent frameworks. In practical terms, marketers and creatives will be able to use Coworker to orchestrate tasks such as creating campaign briefs, evaluating target audiences and producing asset variations for different channels and markets through a single conversational interface rather than switching between multiple tools. Adobe’s Senior Vice President and General Manager of GenStudio and Firefly Enterprise, Varun Parmar, pointed to the scale of content production already flowing through the platform. “Adobe GenStudio has played a central role in helping global brands meet the insatiable demand for content, delivering over 7.8 trillion assets so far this year,” Parmar observed. “Marketing and creative teams now have a mandate to personalise content experiences down to the individual level, and we are reimagining the content supply chain with agentic AI to drive the ‘Studio of the Future’ and bring together impactful creative with deep data insights.” ### Brand Intelligence: teaching AI agents to stay on-brand One of the challenges with deploying AI agents into content workflows is ensuring they produce work that adheres to brand standards. Adobe is addressing this with Brand Intelligence, a continuously learning AI layer that builds knowledge from both written brand guidelines and undocumented institutional knowledge. The company cites a survey of more than 600 marketing and creative professionals that found nearly one-third of public-facing content was estimated to be off-brand. Brand Intelligence is designed to close that gap by providing agents with the brand context they need to make informed decisions as content production scales. Rather than relying solely on static brand guidelines documents, the system is intended to learn from examples and institutional practices, filling in the gaps that formal documentation often misses. [Chinese](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/china/) [embodied AI](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/embodied-ai/) company [Robbyant](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/robbyant/) has released an open-source [AI model](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/ai-model/) designed to give robots a better sense of touch and improve their ability to handle objects. Called LingBot-Touch, the model converts signals from different tactile sensors into a common format that robotic control systems can use. [According to the company](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261109284905/en/Robbyant-Releases-LingBot-Touch-to-Bring-General-Purpose-Touch-Perception-to-Robots), which is part of the [Ant Group](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/ant-group/), trained it on nearly 5,000 hours of real-world tactile data and evaluated it in 26 tests involving two robotic hands and four AI action models. In one test, a Sharpa Wave robotic hand controlled by the T-Rex model successfully unscrewed a bottle cap 56.25% of the time without tactile feedback. Feeding raw sensor signals directly into the action model increased the success rate to 62.5%, while LingBot-Touch raised it to 90%, according to Robbyant. ### Combining Different Types of Touch Sensors Robotic hands use different sensing technologies to detect contact and pressure, but their signals can vary depending on the sensors and how they are arranged. As a result, a model trained to interpret one type of sensor may not work with another, requiring developers to collect additional data and retrain their systems. Robbyant claims LingBot-Touch addresses the problem by processing signals from different sensors through separate encoding pathways and mapping contact points into a shared fingertip coordinate system. The model then interprets contact location, force distribution and how those measurements change over time. Open Source AI.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Robbyant Open-Sources LingBot-Touch: 5,000 Hours [2026] ![Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/tvance.webp) [Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/author/tvance/) Updated Nov 11, 2026 · 17 min read Robbyant, the embodied AI company inside Ant Group, open-sourced LingBot-Touch on November 10, 2026, a tactile foundation model built to give robots a general-purpose sense of touch, according to [its Business Wire release carried by Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20261109284905/robbyant-releases-lingbot-touch-to-bring-general-purpose-touch-perception-to-robots). The model targets one of the stubborn gaps in robotics: machines that see well but still fumble objects the moment contact begins. LingBot-Touch trained on nearly 5,000 hours of real-world tactile data and supports three sensing types: magnetic tactile, visual tactile, and piezoresistive. It encodes signals from all three into a unified tactile representation, so different action models can consume touch data without a custom pipeline for every sensor. Robbyant published a technical report and code, and model resources sit on Hugging Face and GitHub. The launch fits a wider shift toward physical AI, where models leave the chat window and act on the world. Our earlier report on the [ASTRA robot that builds structures in space under DARPA’s NOM4D program](https://shattered.io/astra-robot-builds-structure-in-space-darpa-nom4d-caltech-2026/) showed how much of that work depends on precise contact. This analysis covers what Robbyant confirmed, what remains unverified, how the design compares with other approaches to robot touch perception, and what builders should do next. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. A team picks a gripper, bolts on one type of tactile sensor, collects demonstrations, and trains a policy that only works with that exact hardware. Swap the sensor and the whole pipeline needs new data. That cost keeps tactile sensing out of many production systems, even though contact is where assembly, packing, and household tasks succeed or fail. Robbyant’s answer is a shared layer. LingBot-Touch is described in the announcement as a tactile foundation model, meaning a large pretrained network that other systems build on instead of training from scratch. Its job is to turn raw contact signals into tokens that an action model can read. The company is betting that one pretrained touch encoder can serve many hands and many policies. Open-sourcing the work matters as much as the design. A released technical report and code let outside labs test the claims, port the encoder to their own hardware, and report failures. Closed tactile models can only be judged by the vendor’s own demos. For a field with few shared benchmarks, an open release gives the community something concrete to measure. Open-sourcing the work matters as much as the design. A released technical report and code let outside labs test the claims, port the encoder to their own hardware, and report failures. Closed tactile models can only be judged by the vendor’s own demos. For a field with few shared benchmarks, an open release gives the community something concrete to measure. The Business Wire release and the follow-up coverage agree on the core facts. Infra & Chips.content: [![datacenters logo](/_icons/logos/datacenters-logo-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [AI & Compute Infrastructure](/news/ai-compute-infrastructure) * 2 minRead # SK Telecom, Rebellions, NVIDIA partner for Korea AI infrastructure South Korean firms SK Telecom and Rebellions are collaborating with NVIDIA to advance the country's AI infrastructure. This partnership integrates data centers, processors, and an open infrastructure platform to enhance sovereign AI capabilities. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Nov 10, 2026 at 05:10 PM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Set ETDatacenters as your preferred source on Google") Set ETDatacenters as your preferred source on Google ## Highlights * SK Telecom, Rebellions, and NVIDIA are collaborating on South Korea’s AI infrastructure. * Rebellions will integrate its Rebel R200 NPUs with NVIDIA’s platform via NVLink Fusion. * SK Telecom plans to deploy these integrated systems, drawing on its data center expertise. * South Korea’s government supports this initiative with significant funding for sovereign AI. South Korean telecommunications firm [SK Telecom](/tag/sk+telecom), AI chip startup [Rebellions](/tag/rebellions), and [NVIDIA](/tag/nvidia) have announced a collaboration to advance [South Korea](/tag/south+korea)’s [AI infrastructure](/tag/ai+infrastructure). This initiative aims to integrate [data centers](/tag/data+centers), processors, and an open infrastructure platform. Rebellions will use [NVLink Fusion](/tag/nvlink+fusion) to connect its Rebel R200 neural processing units (NPUs) to NVIDIA’s infrastructure platform. SK Telecom plans to deploy these systems, leveraging its data center expertise, according to a press release from NVIDIA. Jung Jai-hun, SK Telecom Chief Executive Officer and President, stated this collaboration validates the potential of next-generation [sovereign AI](/tag/sovereign+ai) infrastructure. He added it combines global AI infrastructure technology with Korean AI semiconductors. Sunghyun Park, Rebellions co-founder and Chief Executive Officer, noted that Korean technology would lead in powering AI worldwide. Jensen Huang, NVIDIA founder and Chief Executive Officer, highlighted Korea's talent and ambition to be a world leader in AI. The firms plan to develop an approach to disaggregated inference. This will assign different stages of AI response generation to the best-suited processor architecture. The plan includes using NVIDIA GPUs for prefill and Rebellions NPUs for decode to improve inference throughput. ### Government Support and Investment South Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) supports this collaboration to strengthen the country’s sovereign AI infrastructure. Bae Kyung-hoon, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Science and ICT, said this enables Korean-developed NPUs to enter the computing infrastructure market alongside NVIDIA. The government will actively support this collaboration, he added, to deliver tangible results and advance cooperation with NVIDIA. Earlier this month, the South Korean government allocated KRW 21.3 trillion (US$ 15.83 billion) in its budget for 2027. This funding supports the development of physical AI, data centers, and semiconductors. A further KRW 4.7 trillion (US$ 3.5 billion) has been earmarked to develop a sovereign AI model. The government also plans to train 2,000 specialists to lead semiconductor design and the wider chip industry. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?

The collaboration will see Rebellions’ next-generation R200 neural processing units ([NPUs](https://www.eenewseurope.com/en/tags/npu)) integrated into NVIDIA’s MGX rack architecture, with deployment planned at SK Telecom’s AI data centers. The agreement highlights growing opportunities for custom AI accelerators to work alongside NVIDIA GPUs in large-scale inference systems. For European semiconductor developers and data center operators, it offers a potential blueprint for combining domestic AI silicon with established computing infrastructure to support sovereign AI initiatives. ## NVLink Fusion connects custom AI silicon Rebellions plans to use NVIDIA NVLink Fusion to connect its R200 NPUs through high-bandwidth, low-latency networking, targeting energy-efficient inference for frontier AI models, including multitrillion-parameter mixture-of-experts architectures. The NVIDIA MGX rack architecture will provide standardized system designs, while its ecosystem of original design manufacturers and component suppliers could help Rebellions accelerate development and reduce deployment complexity. “Today’s announcement marks a turning point, opening a new chapter for sovereign AI by connecting Korea’s AI silicon and models with global systems technology,” said Sunghyun Park, cofounder and CEO of Rebellions. The companies also plan to explore disaggregated inference, splitting AI workloads between different processor architectures. Under the proposed approach, NVIDIA GPUs would handle the compute-intensive prefill stage, while Rebellions NPUs would manage token generation during decoding. This division of labor is intended to improve inference throughput and power efficiency, potentially addressing two major challenges facing AI data center operators. ## SK Telecom targets full-stack sovereign AI SK Telecom plans to deploy the systems within its AI data center infrastructure, connecting the hardware with proprietary foundation models, including A.X K2, and public-facing AI services. The initiative supports Korea’s government-backed “AI for All” project and aims to strengthen domestic control over AI infrastructure, models and services. Standardizing rack footprints, power delivery and cooling through NVIDIA MGX could also simplify integration of GPU and NPU systems within existing data center environments. ## Government backing and 2028 deployment Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT is supporting the collaboration as part of a broader effort to strengthen the country’s sovereign AI capabilities and domestic semiconductor industry.
